EXT_G5_FP_2018_019.q: A shopkeeper buys 6 dozens of long books. He sold 3 dozen at 150 rupees per dozen and the other 3 dozen at 200 rupees per dozen. Finally he made a profit of 180 rupees. At what rate per dozen did he buy the long books?
hints: Find the total he got from selling. Then cost price equals selling price minus profit. Finally share the cost over 6 dozens.
Cost price equals selling price minus profit.
steps: Selling price equals 3 times 150, plus 3 times 200. That is 450 plus 600, which is 1050 rupees.
Cost price equals 1050 minus 180, which is 870 rupees for 6 dozen.
Cost per dozen equals 870 divided by 6, which is 145 rupees.

EXT_G5_FP_2018_030.q: An article costing 800 rupees is sold at a discount of 20 percent. What was its sale price?
hints: Find 20 percent of 800, the discount. Then subtract it from 800.
Sale price equals price minus discount. Or 80 percent of the price.
steps: 20 percent of 800 equals 160.
Sale price equals 800 minus 160, which is 640 rupees.

EXT_G5_FP_2018_031.q: In how many years will 4000 rupees double at the rate of 12.5 percent simple interest?
hints: Double means the interest earned equals the principal, 4000 rupees. How much interest does 4000 rupees earn in one year at 12.5 percent?
Time equals simple interest times 100, divided by, open bracket, principal times rate, close bracket. Here simple interest equals principal.
steps: To double, simple interest equals 4000 rupees.
Interest per year equals 12.5 percent of 4000, which is 500 rupees.
Years equals 4000 divided by 500, which is 8 years.

EXT_G5_FP_2018_035.q: Each test at a class is for 80 marks. Total 5 tests were to be conducted. A student has scored 30 percent marks at the first 4 tests. To have a score of 35 percent marks on 5 tests, how many marks must he score in the 5th test?
hints: Find the total marks of all 5 tests and the marks he needs for 35 percent. Then find what he already has from the first 4 tests, 30 percent of their total.
Needed in last test equals target total minus marks already scored.
steps: Total of 5 tests equals 5 times 80, which is 400. 35 percent of 400 equals 140 marks needed.
First 4 tests total 320 marks; 30 percent of 320 equals 96 scored.
5th test equals 140 minus 96, which is 44 marks.

EXT_G5_FP_2019_002.q: When an article was sold for 407 rupees the shopkeeper makes a profit of 10 percent. What was the cost price of the article?
hints: A 10 percent profit means the selling price is 110 percent of the cost price. Find 1 percent first.
Cost price equals selling price times 100, divided by, open bracket, 100 plus profit percent, close bracket.
steps: 110 percent of cost price equals 407, so 1 percent equals 407 divided by 110, which is 3.7.
Cost price equals 3.7 times 100, which is 370 rupees.

EXT_G5_FP_2019_004.q: What sum of money will yield an interest of 189 rupees in 3 years at 9 percent per year simple interest?
hints: Use principal equals simple interest times 100, divided by, open bracket, rate times time, close bracket. First work out rate times time, which is 9 times 3.
Principal equals simple interest times 100, divided by, open bracket, rate times time, close bracket.
steps: Rate times time equals 9 times 3, which is 27.
Principal equals 189 times 100, divided by 27. That is 18900 divided by 27, which is 700 rupees.
Check: 9 percent of 700 is 63 a year. Times 3, that is 189. It matches.

EXT_G5_FP_2019_016.q: If 40 percent of the students passed the exam, and the number of unsuccessful students were 420. How many students appeared for the exam?
hints: If 40 percent passed, what percent did not pass? 420 students are that percent.
Fail percent equals 100 percent minus pass percent. Find 1 percent then 100 percent.
steps: Failed equals 100 percent minus 40 percent. That is 60 percent, which is 420 students.
1 percent equals 420 divided by 60, which is 7.
100 percent equals 700 students.

EXT_G5_FP_2019_025.q: A student scored 72 percent on a test of 25 questions. How many of his answers were not correct?
hints: First find how many answers he got right: that is 72 percent of 25. The rest are the ones he did not get right.
72 percent of 25 means 72 times 25, divided by 100. Work that out, then take it away from 25.
A similar one: 80 percent on a test of 20 questions. Right answers: 80 times 20, divided by 100, equals 16. Not right: 20 minus 16 equals 4.
steps: He got 72 percent of the 25 answers right: 72 times 25, divided by 100, equals 18.
The rest were not correct: 25 minus 18 equals 7. So 7 of his answers were not correct.

EXT_G5_FP_2019_031.q: If 3200 rupees amounts to 3680 rupees in 3 years, then what is the rate of interest?
hints: Amount minus principal equals interest. Then use rate equals simple interest times 100, divided by, open bracket, principal times time, close bracket.
Rate equals simple interest times 100, divided by, open bracket, principal times time, close bracket.
steps: Simple interest equals 3680 minus 3200, which is 480 rupees.
Rate equals 480 times 100, divided by, open bracket, 3200 times 3, close bracket. That is 48000 divided by 9600, which is 5 percent.

EXT_G5_FP_2019_035.q: A shopkeeper bought a pen for 40 rupees and wishes to sell it at a profit of 25 percent. What price should he sell the pen for?
hints: 25 percent is one quarter. Find a quarter of 40 and add it to the cost price.
Selling price equals cost price plus profit.
steps: Profit equals 25 percent of 40, which is 10 rupees.
Selling price equals 40 plus 10, which is 50 rupees.

EXT_G5_FP_2020_003.q: If 20 percent of an electricity bill is deducted, then 100 rupees is still to be paid. How much was the original bill?
hints: If 20 percent is taken off, what percent of the bill is left to pay? 100 rupees is that percent.
Whole equals part divided by percent, times 100.
steps: Left to pay equals 100 percent minus 20 percent. That is 80 percent of the bill, which is 100 rupees.
1 percent equals 100 divided by 80, which is 1.25 rupees.
100 percent equals 125 rupees.

EXT_G5_FP_2020_012.q: In April Harry bought a saddle for his horse for 100 rupees. In May he sold it for 200 rupees. In June he was sorry he had sold it, so he bought it back for 300 rupees. In July he got tired of it, so he sold it for 400 rupees. Which of the following is the true outcome of his transactions?
hints: Add up all the money he received when selling and all the money he paid when buying. Compare.
Profit equals total money received minus total money spent.
steps: Money spent when buying equals 100 plus 300, which is 400 rupees.
Money received when selling equals 200 plus 400, which is 600 rupees.
Profit equals 600 minus 400, which is 200 rupees.

EXT_G5_FP_2020_018.q: In what time will 25 rupees become 37 rupees at 16 percent per year simple interest?
hints: Find the interest needed, 37 minus 25. Then find how much interest 25 rupees earns in one year at 16 percent.
Time equals simple interest times 100, divided by, open bracket, principal times rate, close bracket.
steps: Simple interest needed equals 37 minus 25, which is 12 rupees.
Interest in 1 year equals 16 percent of 25, which is 4 rupees.
Time equals 12 divided by 4, which is 3 years.

EXT_G5_FP_2020_030.q: Kedar borrowed 12000 rupees from his friend at simple interest. He returned his friend 15600 rupees in full settlement of his loan after 5 years. What was the rate of interest charged by his friend?
hints: 15600 rupees is the amount, principal plus interest. Subtract to find the interest. Then rate equals simple interest times 100, divided by, open bracket, principal times time, close bracket.
Rate equals simple interest times 100, divided by, open bracket, principal times time, close bracket.
steps: Simple interest equals 15600 minus 12000, which is 3600 rupees.
Rate equals 3600 times 100, divided by, open bracket, 12000 times 5, close bracket. That is 360000 divided by 60000, which is 6 percent per year.

EXT_G5_FP_2020_032.q: What is 5 percent of 5 percent of 100 rupees?
hints: Do it in two steps: first 5 percent of 100, then 5 percent of that answer.
Percent of a percent: work out one step at a time.
steps: Work in two stages. First, 5 percent of 100 rupees is 5 rupees.
Now find 5 percent of 5 rupees: 5 times 5, divided by 100, equals 0.25.
So the answer is 0.25 rupees.

EXT_G5_FP_2020_034.q: A shopkeeper sold a bat for 600 rupees making a profit of 20 percent. What was the cost price of the bat?
hints: With 20 percent profit, 600 rupees is 120 percent of the cost price. Find 1 percent first.
Cost price equals selling price times 100, divided by, open bracket, 100 plus profit percent, close bracket.
steps: 120 percent of cost price equals 600, so 1 percent equals 5.
Cost price equals 5 times 100, which is 500 rupees.

EXT_G5_FP_2021_002.q: A man buys 1000 candy bars at a price of 5 for 2 rupees. He sells all the candy bars at a price of 2 for 1 rupee. What was his profit or loss percent?
hints: Find the total cost: 1000 bars in groups of 5 at 2 rupees each group. Then the total selling price: groups of 2 at 1 rupee. Compare.
Profit percent equals, open bracket, selling price minus cost price, close bracket, divided by cost price, times 100.
steps: Cost price: 1000 divided by 5 is 200 groups. Times 2 rupees, that is 400 rupees.
Selling price: 1000 divided by 2 is 500 groups. Times 1 rupee, that is 500 rupees.
Profit equals 500 minus 400, which is 100 rupees.
Profit percent equals 100 divided by 400, times 100, which is 25 percent profit.

EXT_G5_FP_2021_034.q: Aniket borrowed 18000 rupees to open a grocery shop. He cleared off the loan by paying 25,560 rupees at the end of 3 years. Find the rate of interest.
hints: 25,560 rupees is the amount, principal plus interest. Subtract to get the interest, then rate equals simple interest times 100, divided by, open bracket, principal times time, close bracket.
Rate equals simple interest times 100, divided by, open bracket, principal times time, close bracket.
steps: Simple interest equals 25560 minus 18000, which is 7560 rupees.
Rate equals 7560 times 100, divided by, open bracket, 18000 times 3, close bracket. That is 756000 divided by 54000, which is 14 percent per year.

EXT_G5_FP_2022_005.q: The simple interest earned on a certain principal at 8 percent per year in 5 years is 160 rupees. What is the principal amount?
hints: Rate times time equals 8 times 5, which is 40, so the interest is 40 percent of the principal. If 40 percent equals 160, what is 100 percent?
Principal equals simple interest times 100, divided by, open bracket, rate times time, close bracket.
steps: Rate times time equals 8 times 5, which is 40.
Principal equals 160 times 100, divided by 40, which is 400 rupees.
Check: 8 percent of 400 is 32 a year. Times 5, that is 160. It matches.

EXT_G5_FP_2022_011.q: An article worth 400 rupees is sold for 324 rupees. Find the loss percent.
hints: First find the loss in rupees, cost price minus selling price. Then loss percent equals loss divided by cost price, times 100.
Loss percent equals loss divided by cost price, times 100.
steps: Loss equals 400 minus 324, which is 76 rupees.
Loss percent equals 76 divided by 400, times 100, which is 19 percent.

EXT_G5_FP_2022_015.q: An M B A student has to secure 40 percent marks to pass. He scores 94 marks and fails by 74 marks. Find the maximum marks.
hints: Fails by 74 means he needed 74 more marks. So the passing marks equals 94 plus 74. That is 40 percent of the maximum.
Whole equals part divided by percent, times 100.
steps: Passing marks equals 94 plus 74, which is 168.
40 percent of the maximum equals 168, so 1 percent equals 4.2.
Maximum marks equals 4.2 times 100, which is 420.

EXT_G5_FP_2022_022.q: If 26500 rupees is deposited in a bank at 8 percent per year simple interest, what will be the amount at the end of 4 years?
hints: Find the interest first, principal times rate times time, divided by 100. The amount is the principal plus the interest.
Amount equals principal plus simple interest.
steps: 1 percent of 26500 equals 265. At 8 percent per year, that is 2120.
For 4 years: 2120 times 4 equals 8480 rupees.
Amount equals 26500 plus 8480, which is 34980 rupees.

EXT_G5_FP_2022_031.q: A man buys a mobile phone for 18000 rupees. He wants to make a profit of 18 percent on selling it. Find the selling price of the mobile phone.
hints: Find 18 percent of 18000, that is the profit. Add it to the cost price.
Selling price equals cost price plus profit.
steps: 1 percent of 18000 equals 180. 18 percent equals 18 times 180, which is 3240.
Selling price equals 18000 plus 3240, which is 21240 rupees.

EXT_G5_FP_2022_037.q: 15 percent of 40 minus 25 percent of A equals 2. Find the value of A.
hints: Work out 15 percent of 40 first. Then ask: 6 minus what equals 2? That what is 25 percent of A.
25 percent equals one quarter. If one quarter of A equals 4, then A equals 4 times 4.
steps: 15 percent of 40 equals 6.
6 minus 25 percent of A equals 2, so 25 percent of A equals 4.
A equals 4 times 4, which is 16.

EXT_G5_FP_2023_007.q: Z plus 16 percent of 150 equals 13 percent of 600. Find the value of Z.
hints: Work out the two percentages first: 1 percent of 150 is 1.5 and 1 percent of 600 is 6.
X percent of N equals x times, N divided by 100.
steps: 1 percent of 150 is 1.5, so 16 percent of 150 is 16 times 1.5, which is 24.
1 percent of 600 is 6, so 13 percent of 600 is 13 times 6, which is 78.
So Z plus 24 equals 78, which gives Z equals 78 minus 24, which is 54.

EXT_G5_FP_2023_009.q: If 6420 rupees amounts to 10,272 rupees in 4 years at simple interest, then what is the rate of interest per annum?
hints: Amount minus principal equals interest. Then rate equals simple interest times 100, divided by, open bracket, principal times time, close bracket.
Rate equals simple interest times 100, divided by, open bracket, principal times time, close bracket.
steps: Interest equals amount minus principal: 10272 minus 6420 equals 3852, so the simple interest is 3852 rupees.

Rate equals simple interest times 100, divided by, open bracket, principal times time, close bracket. That is 3852 times 100, divided by, open bracket, 6420 times 4, close bracket. That equals 385200 divided by 25680, which is 15.
So the rate is 15 percent per annum. 15 percent is not one of the choices given, so the answer is none of these.

EXT_G5_FP_2023_019.q: What principal amount will earn an interest of 2205 rupees in 12 months at 18 percent per year simple interest?
hints: 12 months equals 1 year. So 18 percent of the principal is 2205 rupees. Find 1 percent first.
Principal equals simple interest times 100, divided by, open bracket, rate times time, close bracket.
steps: Time equals 1 year. 18 percent of the principal equals 2205.
1 percent equals 2205 divided by 18, which is 122.5.
Principal equals 122.5 times 100, which is 12,250 rupees.

EXT_G5_FP_2023_023.q: If an article is sold for 336 rupees, the loss is 84 rupees. Find the profit if the same article is sold for 542 rupees.
hints: Loss equals cost price minus selling price, so cost price equals selling price plus loss. Find the cost price, then compare it with 542 rupees.
Cost price equals selling price plus loss. Profit equals selling price minus cost price.
steps: A loss means the cost price is more than the selling price: 336 plus 84 equals 420, so the cost price is 420 rupees.
Sold for 542 rupees, the profit is 542 minus 420, which is 122, that is 122 rupees.
122 rupees is not one of the choices given, so the answer is none of these.

EXT_G5_FP_2023_024.q: In how much time will 450 rupees become four times of itself at 24 percent per year simple interest?
hints: If the money becomes 4 times, the interest earned is 3 times the principal, 4 minus 1. Find the interest per year at 24 percent.
Time equals simple interest divided by interest per year.
steps: Simple interest needed equals 3 times 450, which is 1350 rupees.
Interest per year equals 24 percent of 450, which is 108 rupees.
Time equals 1350 divided by 108. That is 12.5 years, which is 12 years 6 months.

EXT_G5_FP_2023_032.q: An article is sold for 12 percent loss. If the loss is 60 rupees, find the profit percent if the same article is sold at 620 rupees.
hints: 12 percent of the cost price is 60 rupees. Find the cost price, 1 percent first. Then work out the profit when sold at 620 rupees.
Profit percent equals, open bracket, selling price minus cost price, close bracket, divided by cost price, times 100.
steps: The loss of 60 rupees is 12 percent of the cost price. So 1 percent of the cost price is 60 divided by 12, which is 5, and the cost price is 100 times 5, which is 500, that is 500 rupees.
Sold at 620 rupees, the profit is 620 minus 500, which is 120, that is 120 rupees.
Profit percent: 120 divided by 500, times 100, equals 24, so the profit is 24 percent.
24 percent is not one of the choices given, so the answer is none of these.

EXT_G5_FP_2023_033.q: What percent is 84 minutes of 7 hours?
hints: Make the units the same: change 7 hours into minutes. Then part divided by whole, times 100.
Percent equals part divided by whole, times 100. 1 hour equals 60 minutes.
steps: 7 hours equals 7 times 60, which is 420 minutes.
84 divided by 420, times 100, equals 20 percent.

EXT_G5_FP_2024_002.q: If an article is sold at 440 rupees, the profit percent is 10 percent. At what price should it be sold so that the profit percent is 17 percent?
hints: Selling price of 440 is 110 percent of the cost price. Find the cost price first, find 1 percent, then work out 117 percent of it.

Cost price equals selling price times 100, divided by, open bracket, 100 plus profit percent, close bracket. New selling price equals cost price times, open bracket, 100 plus new profit percent, close bracket, divided by 100.
steps: A 10 percent profit means 440 rupees is 110 percent of the cost price.
So 1 percent of the cost price is 440 divided by 110, which is 4, and the cost price is 100 times 4, which is 400, that is 400 rupees.
For a 17 percent profit the selling price is 117 percent of the cost price: 117 times 4 equals 468.
So it should be sold for 468 rupees.

EXT_G5_FP_2024_015.q: If 28 percent of a number is 196. Find 43 percent of that same number.
hints: If 28 percent is 196, what is 1 percent? Then multiply by 43.
Find 1 percent first, then multiply.
steps: 1 percent equals 196 divided by 28, which is 7.
43 percent equals 43 times 7, which is 301.

EXT_G5_FP_2024_017.q: Medha borrowed 3500 rupees from a friend at simple interest. After 3 years she repaid the loan by giving 4340 rupees. What was the rate of interest per annum?
hints: The amount repaid includes the borrowed money plus interest. Subtract to find the interest, then use simple interest equals principal times rate times time, divided by 100, to find the rate.
Simple interest equals amount minus principal. Rate equals simple interest times 100, divided by, open bracket, principal times time, close bracket.
steps: Simple interest equals 4340 minus 3500, which is 840 rupees.
Rate equals 840 times 100, divided by, open bracket, 3500 times 3, close bracket. That is 84000 divided by 10500, which is 8 percent.

EXT_G5_FP_2024_024.q: A dealer bought 26 cricket bats at 1250 rupees per bat. He sold 14 of them at 1800 rupees each and the remaining bats at 825 rupees each. Find profit percent or loss percent in the overall transaction.
hints: Find total cost, then total selling price, in two parts! Remember, 26 minus 14 bats are left for the second price.
Profit percent equals, open bracket, selling price minus cost price, close bracket, divided by cost price, times 100.
steps: Total cost price equals 26 times 1250, which is 32,500 rupees.
Selling price equals 14 times 1800, plus 12 times 825. That is 25,200 plus 9,900, which is 35,100 rupees.
Profit equals 35,100 minus 32,500, which is 2,600 rupees.
Profit percent equals 2600 divided by 32500, times 100, which is 8 percent profit.

EXT_G5_FP_2024_026.q: Mishti scored 44 out of 50 in Science, 50 out of 50 in Mathematics, 42 out of 50 in English and 84 out of 100 in Social Science. Find her overall percentage in the final exam.
hints: Add up all marks she got, add up all the maximum marks, and then do scored divided by total, times 100.
Percentage equals marks scored divided by total marks, times 100.
steps: Scored: 44 plus 50 plus 42 plus 84 equals 220.
Total: 50 plus 50 plus 50 plus 100 equals 250.
220 divided by 250, times 100, equals 88 percent.

EXT_G5_FP_2024_038.q: Calculate Simple Interest on 4250 rupees for 5 years at 8 percent per year rate of interest.
hints: Use simple interest equals principal times rate times time, divided by 100. Try finding 1 percent of 4250 first.
Simple interest equals principal times rate times time, divided by 100.
steps: 1 percent of 4250 equals 42.5.
Per year at 8 percent, that is 8 times 42.5, which is 340.
For 5 years, that is 5 times 340, which is 1700 rupees.

EXT_G5_FP_2025_005.q: What percent of 80 should be added to 80 so as to get the sum equal to the square of 12?
hints: What is 12 times 12? How much extra do you need on top of 80? Then ask: that extra is what percent of 80?
Percent equals part divided by whole, times 100.
steps: Square of 12 equals 144.
Extra needed equals 144 minus 80, which is 64.
64 divided by 80, times 100, equals 80 percent.

EXT_G5_FP_2025_006.q: An article is sold at a loss of 80 rupees. If the article was sold at 375 rupees the profit would have been twice the loss. Find at what price the article was sold.
hints: Profit would be twice the loss, which is 2 times 80, that is 160 rupees. Use that to find the cost price first.
Cost price equals selling price minus profit. And selling price at a loss equals cost price minus loss.
steps: Profit would be 2 times 80, which is 160 rupees, at a selling price of 375 rupees.
Cost price equals 375 minus 160, which is 215 rupees.
The original selling price, at a loss of 80 rupees, equals 215 minus 80, which is 135 rupees.

EXT_G5_FP_2025_007.q: Find the rate of interest if 28500 rupees amounts to 38760 rupees in three years.
hints: Amount equals principal plus interest. Find the interest first, then use rate equals simple interest times 100, divided by, open bracket, principal times time, close bracket.
Rate equals simple interest times 100, divided by, open bracket, principal times time, close bracket.
steps: Simple interest equals 38,760 minus 28,500, which is 10,260 rupees.
Rate equals 10,260 times 100, divided by, open bracket, 28,500 times 3, close bracket. That is 1,026,000 divided by 85,500, which is 12 percent per annum.

EXT_G5_FP_2025_020.q: 6.5 percent of 800 equals 8 percent of 250 plus M. Find the value of M.
hints: Work out each percentage separately: 1 percent of 800 is 8, and 1 percent of 250 is 2.5.
X percent of N equals x times, N divided by 100.
steps: 1 percent of 800 is 8, so 6.5 percent of 800 is 6.5 times 8, which is 52.
1 percent of 250 is 2.5, so 8 percent of 250 is 8 times 2.5, which is 20.
So 52 equals 20 plus M, which gives M equals 52 minus 20, which is 32.

EXT_G5_FP_2025_024.q: By selling an article for 78 rupees, a loss of 35 percent is made. For how much should the article be sold to make a profit of 15 percent?
hints: A 35 percent loss means 78 rupees is only 65 percent of the cost price. Find cost price, then take 115 percent of it.

Selling price equals cost price times, open bracket, 100 minus loss percent, close bracket, divided by 100. So cost price equals selling price times 100, divided by, open bracket, 100 minus loss percent, close bracket.
steps: A 35 percent loss means 78 rupees is only 65 percent of the cost price, because 100 minus 35 equals 65.
So 1 percent of the cost price is 78 divided by 65, which is 1.2, and the cost price is 100 times 1.2, which is 120, that is 120 rupees.
For a 15 percent profit the selling price is 115 percent of the cost price: 115 times 1.2 equals 138.
So it should be sold for 138 rupees.

EXT_G5_FP_2025_026.q: What amount will you have to invest to earn simple interest of 280 rupees per month at 15 percent per year rate of interest?
hints: The rate is per year but the interest is per month. Convert 280 rupees a month into a yearly interest first.
Principal equals simple interest times 100, divided by, open bracket, rate times time, close bracket.
steps: Interest in 1 year equals 280 times 12, which is 3360 rupees.
Principal equals 3360 times 100, divided by, open bracket, 15 times 1, close bracket. That is 336000 divided by 15, which is 22,400 rupees.

EXT_G5_FP_2025_040.q: Find simple interest if 16000 rupees is invested for 18 months at 8 percent per year.
hints: Time must be in years. How many years is 18 months?
18 months equals 1.5 years. Simple interest equals principal times rate times time, divided by 100.
steps: Time equals 18 divided by 12, which is 1.5 years.
1 percent of 16000 equals 160. At 8 percent for 1 year, that is 1280.
For 1.5 years: 1280 times 1.5 equals 1920 rupees.

EXT_G5_WS_B2_024.q: In an account statement, an expenditure of 600 rupees was considered as income by mistake. As a result, the cash balance was 15000 rupees. If the error is corrected, the cash balance will be?
hints: If expenditure was wrongly added as income, we need to reverse the error.
Wrongly added 600, should have subtracted. To correct: subtract 600 twice, once to remove wrong addition, once to apply correct subtraction.
Try: Balance shown equals 100. 10 rupees expenditure shown as income. Correct balance equals 100 minus 10 minus 10, which is 80.
steps: 600 rupees was spent, so it should have been taken away from the balance. By mistake it was added instead.
First undo the mistaken addition: 15000 minus 600 equals 14400.
Then take away the 600 rupees that was really spent: 14400 minus 600 equals 13800. So the correct cash balance is 13800 rupees.

EXT_G5_WS_B2_025.q: In an account statement, an income of 600 rupees was written as expenditure by mistake. As a result, the cash balance was 15000 rupees. If the error is corrected, the cash balance will be?
hints: 600 rupees was money coming in, so it should have been added to the balance. By mistake it was taken away instead.
Fix it in two moves. First add 600 rupees back to 15000 to undo the mistake. Then add 600 rupees once more, because the income still has to be counted.
Example: a balance shows 100 rupees after an income of 10 rupees was written as spending. Undo the mistake: 100 plus 10 equals 110. Count the income: 110 plus 10 equals 120 rupees.
steps: 600 rupees was income, so it should have been added to the balance. By mistake it was taken away instead.
First undo the mistaken subtraction: 15000 plus 600 equals 15600.
Then add the 600 rupees income that was never counted: 15600 plus 600 equals 16200. So the correct cash balance is 16200 rupees.

VAR2_EXT_G5_WS_01_006_01.q: Neha buys 4 pens at 10 rupees each and pays 50 rupees. How much change does Neha get back?

VAR2_EXT_G5_WS_01_006_02.q: Nikhil buys a bag for 100 rupees and sells it at a profit of 15 percent. What is the selling price?

Profit equals 15 over 100, times 100.
steps: Profit equals 15 percent of 100 rupees, which is 15 rupees.
Selling price equals cost price plus profit. That is 100 plus 15, which equals 115 rupees.

VAR2_EXT_G5_WS_01_006_03.q: Riya bought a laptop for 300 rupees and sold it at a loss of 15 percent. What is the selling price?
hints: Find 15 percent of the cost price.
Selling price equals cost price minus loss.
Loss means sold for less than bought.
steps: Loss equals 15 percent of 300 rupees, which is 45 rupees.
Selling price equals cost price minus loss. That is 300 minus 45, which equals 255 rupees.

VAR2_EXT_G5_WS_01_006_04.q: If 8 sharpeners cost 24 rupees, what is the cost of one sharpener?
hints: To find the price of one item, divide total cost by quantity.
Total cost is 24 rupees for 8 items.
Divide 24 by 8.
steps: Cost of 1 equals total divided by quantity.
That equals 24 rupees divided by 8, which is 3 rupees.

VAR2_EXT_G5_WS_B2_006_01.q: Vivek buys 8 erasers at 6 rupees each and pays 63 rupees. How much change does Vivek get back?
hints: First find the total cost: price times quantity.
Then subtract from what Vivek paid.
